facts.text: Arden was founded in 1900 by sculptor Frank Stephens and architect William Lightfoot Price as a radical Georgist single‑tax community.
Six of William Lightfoot Price’s Elizabethan Revival cottages—Friendly Gables, The Lodge, Rest Cottage, Green Gate, The Second Homestead, and The Fels House—still line Arden’s streets.
Arden’s historic Mayday and Midsummer festivals blend folk tradition with the town’s early commitment to progressive social values.
The Arden Craft Shop, established in the early 1900s, preserves hand‑craft traditions that were central to the community’s Arts and Crafts‑influenced founding vision.
In 1973, the entire village of Arden was listed on the National Register of Historic Places, recognizing its unique cultural landscape.
Arden’s founding principles—community governance, land reform, and environmental stewardship—continue to shape local policies and initiatives today.
